prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a close-range kitchen sink area where overhanging upper cabinets (bright, roughly 0.2 to 0.4 m above and in front of the camera wearer) jut out over a recessed backsplash wall and sink basin (darker, about 0.5 to 0.8 m away). Along the bottom and right, brighter silhouettes mark objects within arm's reach (0.2 to 0.5 m): a white container at bottom-center with the wearer's reaching right hand beside it in frame 2, another person's head entering at the bottom-left edge in frames 2 to 5 (about 0.2 to 0.3 m to the wearer's left, facing the sink rather than the wearer), and a cluster of upright bottles spaced 0.05 to 0.15 m apart on the right counter. Across the 5 frames, the progressive brightening and upward-left shift of the bottles and upper-left cabinet corner show the camera wearer leaning forward, tilting downward, and turning right toward the counter corner while partially truncating the sink and surrounding clutter at the frame edges. Even during heavy RGB motion blur in frames 1, 3, and 5, the depth map clearly separates the protruding cabinet plane and freestanding bottle silhouettes from the background wall. However, the map is unreliable in frame 1 where the sunlit left wall drops to black as if far away, and in frames 3 to 5 where the flat wall in the upper-left is rendered overly bright as if nearer than the foreground bottles.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of counter objects within arm's reach (0.4 to 0.6 m in front of the camera wearer): a pink 'person' mask in the lower-left of frame 1, a single yellow 'bottle' mask on the right counter in frames 2 and 3, three side-by-side 'bottle' masks (cyan, yellow, and brown, 0.05 to 0.1 m apart) below the wall outlet in frame 4, and nothing in frame 5. From frame 2 to frame 4, the bottle masks enlarge and shift from the bottom-right toward the center as the camera wearer approaches and turns right, before disappearing in frame 5. In frame 4, the distinct coloured masks clearly separate the overlapping purple bottle, translucent blue soap bottle, and red-capped bottle that visually merge against the shadowed counter in the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable: in frame 1 it misclassifies sunlit dish clutter as a 'person', and across frames 2 to 5 it completely misses the actual person's head at the bottom-left edge (0.2 to 0.3 m away, facing the sink) as well as the wearer's reaching hand in frame 2. It also fails to segment the cabinets, sink, sponge, white container, and all objects during the motion-blurred fifth frame.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, detecting no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's right hand and forearm briefly enter at the bottom-center of frame 2 within 0.3 m of the camera to reach a white container, while a second person's dark hair and top of the head appear at the bottom-left edge in frames 2 to 5, roughly 0.2 to 0.3 m to the wearer's left and below eye level. That second person is positioned beside the wearer facing forward toward the sink rather than looking at the camera, and stays near the lower-left corner as the wearer leans closer to the right counter across frames 2 to 5. Because the camera is pitched toward the upper cabinets and close counter (0.3 to 0.7 m away), nearly all of both people's bodies and limbs lie outside the field of view or are truncated by the bottom frame boundary. Consequently, the pose map adds no spatial cues beyond the RGB frames and is unreliable for close-up egocentric views where hands and heads are heavily cropped and blurred by motion.
